summary: RedCap is a mature local skill-root runtime with a CLI facade, package safety gate and clean workspace E2E, but it is not yet an excellent public npm CLI/runtime product. Before public release, the runtime/project/user boundaries, workspace context contract, public package identity, license posture, CLI debug contract and public knowledge claims need remediation or explicit scope reduction.

observed_facts.source_visibility_model: npm package source must be treated as visible to users

findings.claim: The current package surface passes the publish safety gate, including content scanning for local user home paths, and excludes known local secrets, runtime residue and private knowledge paths.

The current package metadata remains private and uses @redcap-ai/runtime, while the user-approved public package name is @norven63/redcap. This is correct for readiness-only mode but blocks public publish.

The execution-layer split remains dry-run-only. Current runtime implementation still lives in the RedCap skill-root shape, so public CLI release would ship an internal bundle rather than a clean independent runtime layout.
The current CLI facade exposes core commands but does not yet expose publish-grade doctor/debug/trace surfaces. This makes external-user support and Agent-container diagnosis too opaque.

The current CLI defaults status, diagnose and closeout-style task operations to package-root state such as $REDCAP_ROOT/.dev-task.md. A public CLI must operate on the managed project workspace by default, with the npm package acting as runtime implementation rather than the project state directory.
package.json currently declares UNLICENSED. That is acceptable while private=true, but a public npm release needs an explicit distribution/license decision before publish.

The npm package candidate surface currently contains 201 files and many internal governance artifacts. This is acceptable for internal runtime readiness, but should be curated before public product release.
redcap-arsenal currently contains only templates, schema and Norven namespace placeholders. It must not be marketed as a populated shared knowledge/skill arsenal until append-only entries exist.
The release posture now treats npm package contents as visible source and relies on exclusion of secrets rather than obfuscation.
The intended Agent container contract is conceptually clear: invoke CLI at revive/task/check/closeout nodes. A public user guide should still make this concrete before broad release.

must_not_claim: Do not claim RedCap is public-release-ready.
Do not claim P4-2 public release is complete.
Do not claim redcap-arsenal contains substantive migrated knowledge.
Do not claim npm source is hidden from users.
Do not claim clean workspace E2E equals a multi-OS external release matrix.

recommended_next_tranches.title: Runtime/project/user boundary physical split and compatibility shim apply
CLI product command surface hardening: doctor/debug/trace/errors/help
Public package identity and curated package surface preparation
Public arsenal content strategy and claim boundary
